title: URL Versioning
definition: The most common and explicit strategy for API versioning, where the version number is embedded directly into the URL path.
simpleExplanation: You put `/v1/` in the URL. When you need to make breaking changes, you create a new set of endpoints starting with `/v2/`. Both URLs run on the server at the same time.
realWorldExample: Twitter's API. `api.twitter.com/1.1/tweets` uses their old format. `api.twitter.com/2/tweets` uses their completely redesigned modern format.

basic: Give an example of a URL-versioned endpoint.
intermediate: What is the main architectural criticism of URL Versioning among REST purists?

answers.question: Criticism?
answers.answer: REST purists argue that a URL should point to a specific *Resource* (the user). A version is not a resource; it is a representation of the data. Therefore, versioning should theoretically happen in the Headers, not the URL.
